main::run_deep_learning
run_deep_learning(results_dir) is a small orchestration function that launches the project’s deep learning training pipeline. It prints a start message, imports DLTrainer from src.deep_learning.trainer, creates a DLTrainer instance, and calls its train(results_dir) method. After training completes it prints a success message and reports the provided results_dir where outputs are saved. The function has no return value and may raise exceptions if the import or training step fails.

main::run_physics_informed
A small top-level function that launches a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) training run. It prints a start message, imports PINNTrainer from src.physics_informed.trainer, instantiates the trainer, calls trainer.train(results_dir) to perform the training (using the provided results_dir as the output location), and then prints completion and the results directory. The function has no return value and performs I/O via printing and whatever the trainer.train method does (e.g., saving files); it may raise errors from the import or training process.

main::main
Entry-point function for the Magnetic Field Predictor script. It parses a required command-line option --method (choices: 'dl' or 'pinn'), creates a timestamped results directory named results/<TIMESTAMP>_<METHOD>, configures logging to both a training.log file in that directory and the console, prints the results path, and then dispatches to either run_deep_learning(results_dir) or run_physics_informed(results_dir) depending on the chosen method. After the selected routine finishes it prints completion messages. The function performs filesystem and logging side effects and does not return a value.

main::run_attention_model
Starts and runs a full training pipeline for an Attention-based model. Given a configuration dict, a data path and a data type, it: creates a results directory and logging locations, updates the config with tensorboard/log dirs, loads the dataset via DataLoader and prints dataset info, constructs an AttentionModel from model settings in the config, initializes an AttentionTrainer with the model and data loader, runs training and evaluation, prints the final test loss, optionally saves the trained model to the results folder, and returns the trained model object plus the results directory path. The function also emits progress/info messages to stdout and writes logs to the created log directory.

main::create_results_directory
Creates a timestamped results directory under a top-level "results" folder. It builds a directory name using the current local datetime formatted as YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS plus the provided model_type and data_type ("<timestamp>_<model_type>_<data_type>"), ensures the directory (and any missing parent directories) exists, and returns a pathlib.Path to that directory. The call is idempotent (exist_ok=True).

main::setup_logging
Ensures the given log_dir exists, creates a timestamped log file named training_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.log inside it, and configures Python logging to INFO level with a timestamped message format. Logging is directed both to the created file (via logging.FileHandler) and to the console (via logging.StreamHandler). The function returns the Path to the created log file.

main::run_rnn_model
Runs end-to-end training and evaluation of an RNN using the provided configuration and dataset. Specifically, it: creates a results directory and sets up logging; updates the config with log/tensorboard paths; initializes a DataLoader for the specified data_path and data_type and prints dataset info; constructs an RNNModel from the config and wraps it with an RNNTrainer; trains the model and evaluates it to produce a test loss; optionally saves the trained model (controlled by config['logging']['save_model'], default True); prints status messages throughout. It returns the trained model instance and the path to the results directory. The function also mutates the config by inserting log directory paths and produces side effects (files/logs saved to disk).

main::run_q_learning
Starts and runs a Q-Learning optimization session. Given an environment name (string), a configuration object, and a results directory path, the function: (1) prints a start message; (2) instantiates the appropriate environment class (SynRMEnvironment for "synrm", CCoreEnvironment for "ccore"); (3) raises ValueError for unknown environment names; (4) creates a QLearningTrainer with the chosen environment and config; (5) runs trainer.train(results_dir); and (6) prints completion and results-directory messages.

main::run_comparison
Orchestrates a comparison run between two optimization methods (Q-Learning and a Genetic Algorithm) across two environments. It prints a start message, then for each environment in ["synrm", "ccore"] it initializes results[env_name] = {} and iterates over methods ["ql", "ga"]. For method "ql" it calls run_q_learning(env_name, config, results_dir / f"{env_name}_ql"); for "ga" it calls run_genetic_algorithm(env_name, config, results_dir / f"{env_name}_ga"). After running all combinations it prints completion messages and the results directory. Notes: the function has no return value, relies on external globals/functions (results, run_q_learning, run_genetic_algorithm), and uses the provided config and results_dir to dispatch each experiment into a per-environment/method subpath.

main::run_genetic_algorithm
Function run_genetic_algorithm(environment_name, config, results_dir): orchestrates a Genetic Algorithm optimization run. It prints a start message, selects and instantiates an environment object based on the case-insensitive environment_name ('synrm' -> SynRMEnvironment, 'ccore' -> CCoreEnvironment), raises a ValueError for unknown names, constructs a GeneticAlgorithm with the chosen environment and provided config, runs its optimize method saving results to results_dir, and then prints completion and results-location messages.

main::run_a2c
run_a2c(config: dict, results_dir: Path) starts and runs an Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) training session. It prints a start message, imports and instantiates src.a2c.trainer.A2CTrainer with the provided configuration and results directory, calls trainer.train() to execute training, then calls trainer.close(). After training it prints completion and summary statistics taken from the returned results dict (mean reward over the last 10 episodes, best reward, total episodes, and total training time). The function performs the training synchronously and does not return a value.

agent::ProbabilityDistribution
A small tf.keras.Model subclass that implements stochastic action sampling from logits. Its call(logits) uses tf.random.categorical(logits, 1) to draw one categorical sample per batch entry, then tf.squeeze(..., axis=-1) to return a 1-D tensor of sampled action indices (one int index per batch). The returned tensor contains integer class indices (tf.random.categorical produces int64). This is a non-differentiable sampler for converting action logits into sampled discrete actions.

agent::A2CModel
A2CModel is a TensorFlow Keras model implementing the actor–critic (A2C) network used to produce policy logits and value estimates from image-like observations. It is constructed with a num_actions integer and a configuration dict that controls convolutional filters, kernel sizes, strides and hidden layer sizes. The network consists of two convolutional layers followed by a flattening layer, then two separate dense pathways: an actor_hidden dense that feeds a policy_head producing raw action logits (shape: [batch, num_actions]) and a critic_hidden dense that feeds a value_head producing scalar value estimates (shape: [batch, 1]). The model stores a ProbabilityDistribution helper used to sample actions from the returned logits and a logger. The call(inputs) method runs the forward pass and returns (policy_logits, value_estimates). The action_value(observation) convenience method accepts a single observation (adds a batch dimension if needed), runs prediction, samples an action via the ProbabilityDistribution, and returns the sampled action and the corresponding value (both squeezed to remove the extra batch dimension). The class inherits tf.keras.Model and is named 'a2c_model'.

agent::A2CAgent
A2CAgent is an implementation of the Advantage Actor–Critic (A2C) agent that wraps a neural network policy/value model and provides action selection, return/advantage computation, and batched training. On construction it reads hyperparameters from a provided config (gamma, entropy_coefficient, value_coefficient, learning_rate), creates an A2CModel with the environment action dimension, and compiles it with RMSprop and two custom losses (policy and value). get_action(observation) queries the model for a sampled action and its value estimate. compute_returns_and_advantages(rewards, values, dones, next_value) computes discounted returns with episode termination handling and returns advantages as returns minus predicted values. train_step(observations, actions, returns, advantages) packages actions and advantages together and calls model.train_on_batch to update both policy and value heads, returning total, policy and value losses. The policy loss uses SparseCategoricalCrossentropy weighted by advantages plus an entropy term scaled by entropy_coefficient; the value loss is a mean-squared error scaled by value_coefficient. Utility methods save_model, load_model and get_model_summary persist and inspect model weights/architecture.

Although the implementation body is not provided here, its role is to implement the neural network used by the A2C algorithm — typically a shared feature extractor with two output heads: an actor head that produces policy logits or action probabilities and a critic head that predicts state values. In this codebase the class is expected to define the network layers, a call/forward method that returns the policy and value outputs (and possibly a sampled action or distribution), and helper functionality needed by the agent for computing action selection and value estimates during training and inference.

agent::A2CAgent::train_step
Performs a single A2C training update on a batch. The method accepts numpy arrays for observations, actions, discounted returns and advantage estimates. It first concatenates actions and advantages column-wise into a (batch_size, 2) array (actions[:, None] and advantages[:, None]) to form the input expected by the policy loss, then calls self.model.train_on_batch with observations as input and [actions_and_advantages, returns] as the two targets. It returns a dict of floating-point training metrics extracted from the model's returned losses: 'total_loss' (losses[0]), 'policy_loss' (losses[1]) and 'value_loss' (losses[2]). The implementation assumes the model is configured to accept these targets (policy head that uses action+advantage and a value head that regresses to returns).

agent::A2CAgent::_policy_loss
Computes the A2C policy loss with entropy regularization. The function expects a single tensor actions_and_advantages containing actions and their corresponding advantage weights concatenated along the last axis; it splits this into actions (first half) and advantages (second half), casting actions to int32. It computes the policy loss as a weighted sparse categorical cross-entropy (from_logits=True) using advantages as sample weights, and computes the policy entropy by evaluating categorical_crossentropy(logits, logits, from_logits=True) (which yields -sum p log p). The final returned tensor is policy_loss - entropy_coeff * entropy_loss (entropy is subtracted so the optimizer, which minimizes, effectively maximizes entropy).

agent::A2CAgent::save_model
Method of A2CAgent that saves the agent's neural network weights to disk. It calls self.model.save_weights(filepath) using the provided filepath (string) and writes an info-level log via self.logger indicating where the model weights were saved. Note: it saves weights only, not the full model object or architecture.

agent::ProbabilityDistribution::call
Given a tensor of class logits, this method samples one categorical action per row by drawing from the categorical distribution defined by the logits. It calls tf.random.categorical(logits, 1) to produce one sampled index per input row and tf.squeeze(..., axis=-1) to remove the singleton sample dimension, returning an int64 tensor of sampled class indices (shape typically [batch_size] or a scalar for a single example).

agent::A2CModel::__init__
Constructor for the A2CModel that builds and initializes the neural network components used by an Advantage Actor-Critic agent. It accepts the number of discrete actions (num_actions) and a configuration dictionary (config), calls the parent initializer with the name 'a2c_model', and stores the inputs. The constructor creates two convolutional feature-extraction layers (keras.layers.Convolution2D) and a Flatten layer, then defines separate hidden Dense layers for the actor and critic paths using sizes from config['hidden_size']. It adds a value head (Dense(1)) that predicts a scalar state value and a policy logits head (Dense(num_actions)) that produces unnormalized action logits. It also instantiates a ProbabilityDistribution helper for sampling actions and sets up a module logger. The config keys referenced include 'filter_no', 'kernel_size', 'strides', and 'hidden_size', and ReLU activations are used for intermediate layers.

agent::A2CModel::call
Performs the forward pass of an A2C actor-critic model. It accepts an input tensor (expected shape [batch_size, channels, height, width]), converts it to tf.float32, runs it through two convolutional layers and a flattening layer, then splits into separate actor and critic paths. The actor path passes through actor_hidden then policy_head to produce policy logits; the critic path passes through critic_hidden then value_head to produce value estimates. Returns a tuple (policy_logits, value_estimates). Note: policy_logits are raw logits (no softmax applied) and value_estimates are the critic outputs (typically a per-batch scalar). The method relies on the instance layers: conv1, conv2, flatten, actor_hidden, critic_hidden, policy_head, and value_head.

agent::A2CAgent::__init__
Constructor for the A2CAgent class. It stores the provided configuration, creates a logger, reads A2C hyperparameters (gamma, entropy coefficient, value coefficient, learning rate) from the config dictionary, instantiates an A2CModel using the environment action dimension and model config, compiles that model with an RMSprop optimizer and two custom losses (policy and value: self._policy_loss and self._value_loss), and logs that the agent has been initialized. The method initializes the following instance attributes: config, logger, gamma, entropy_coeff, value_coeff, learning_rate, and model.

agent::A2CModel::action_value
For a single environment observation, this method returns a sampled action and the critic value estimate. If the input is a 3-D observation (no batch), it first adds a batch dimension. It then calls self.predict(observation) to obtain policy logits and the value estimate, uses self.dist.predict(logits) to produce an action from the logits, and finally squeezes the trailing singleton dimension(s) from both the action and value outputs before returning (so callers get scalar or 1-D outputs rather than batch-wrapped arrays).

agent::A2CAgent::get_action
A method on A2CAgent that takes a single environment observation (numpy array), asks the agent's model for an action and a value estimate via self.model.action_value(observation), and returns them as a tuple (action as int, value estimate as float). It simply forwards the observation to the model and casts the returned action and value to the specified primitive types.

agent::A2CAgent::compute_returns_and_advantages
compute_returns_and_advantages computes discounted episode returns and simple advantages for a trajectory. Given arrays of rewards, value estimates, and done flags, and an optional next_value for bootstrapping, it builds the returns by backward recursion using returns[t] = rewards[t] + gamma * returns[t+1] * (1 - dones[t]) with the last-step initialized as rewards[-1] + gamma * next_value * (1 - dones[-1]). Advantages are then computed as returns - values. Both outputs are returned as float32 NumPy arrays. This implementation uses the agent's self.gamma and does not implement GAE (it is a plain return-minus-baseline advantage).

agent::A2CAgent::_value_loss
Private method of A2CAgent that computes the value (critic) loss. It calculates the mean squared error between the target returns and the predicted values using kls.mean_squared_error, then scales that MSE by the agent's value_coeff hyperparameter. The result is a scalar/tensor loss used to train the value network.

agent::A2CAgent::load_model
Method of the A2CAgent class that loads saved weights into the agent's neural network. It calls self.model.load_weights(filepath) to restore weights from the given file path and logs an informational message via self.logger. The method does not return a value and will raise an error if the file is missing or incompatible.

agent::A2CAgent::get_model_summary
A simple wrapper method on A2CAgent that forwards to the underlying model's summary() call. It calls and returns self.model.summary(), which prints the model architecture to stdout (and typically returns None for standard Keras/TensorFlow models) — no parameters.

trainer::A2CTrainer
A2CTrainer is a training manager for an Advantage Actor‑Critic (A2C) agent. It initializes logging, a CcoreFemmEnv environment and an A2CAgent from a provided configuration, and exposes a train() method that runs the main training loop until configured episode or update limits are reached. During training it repeatedly collects fixed-size experience batches (_collect_batch), computes returns and advantages and performs agent updates (_train_agent), evaluates the agent periodically in a separate evaluation environment (_evaluate_agent), and saves model checkpoints and final training artifacts. It records metrics (episode rewards/lengths, per‑update training metrics, evaluation results), compiles and JSON‑serializes results (converting numpy types) to training_results.json, and writes logs and render outputs to the results directory. Utility methods include checkpoint saving (_save_checkpoint), result compilation (_compile_results), serialization helper (_make_serializable), and close() to release the environment. Configurable behavior is driven by entries such as max_episodes, max_updates, batch_size, play_interval and save_frequency.

trainer::A2CTrainer::_train_agent
_Trains the A2C agent on a single collected experience batch and returns training metrics._ Given a batch_data dictionary (containing 'observations', 'actions', 'rewards', 'values', 'dones', and 'next_value'), the method: 1) computes discounted returns and advantages by calling self.agent.compute_returns_and_advantages with rewards, values, dones and next_value; 2) performs a training step via self.agent.train_step using observations, actions, the computed returns and advantages and receives training metrics; 3) augments the returned metrics with summary statistics (mean_reward, mean_value, mean_advantage) and the batch_size (len(observations)); and 4) returns the combined metrics dictionary.

trainer::A2CTrainer::train
Runs the main A2C training loop for the trainer instance. It initializes the environment and then repeatedly collects experience batches via _collect_batch, trains the agent on non-empty batches via _train_agent (incrementing update_count), and tracks per-update training metrics. It increments episode_count when a batch indicates the episode finished, records episode rewards and lengths, resets the environment for new episodes, and otherwise appends the next observation to obs_history. Periodically (every play_interval updates) it runs _evaluate_agent and stores evaluation results, and it saves model checkpoints every save_frequency episodes via _save_checkpoint. The loop exits when either max_episodes or max_updates is reached. After finishing it performs a final evaluation, compiles and saves results with _compile_results and _save_results, logs timing information, and returns the results dictionary. The method uses instance lists (training_metrics, evaluation_results, episode_rewards, episode_lengths) and the logger for progress reporting.

trainer::A2CTrainer::_save_checkpoint
Creates a checkpoint file for the trainer's agent by saving the agent model to disk. It ensures a 'checkpoints' folder exists under self.results_dir, builds a filename of the form 'model_ep{episode}_up{update}.h5', calls self.agent.save_model(...) with that path, and logs an informational message. This method has no return value and has side effects on the filesystem and the trainer's logger.

trainer::A2CTrainer::_save_results
Private method that writes a training-results dictionary to disk as JSON. It builds the path results_dir/'training_results.json', converts any non-JSON-native objects (e.g., numpy arrays) to serializable forms via self._make_serializable, dumps the resulting structure to the file with indent=2, and logs an info message indicating where the results were saved. Uses self.results_dir and self.logger.

trainer::A2CTrainer::__init__
Constructor for the A2CTrainer class. It stores the provided configuration and results directory (converting to a pathlib.Path and creating the directory), configures Python logging (file handler to results_dir/training.log and a stream handler, using log level from config), creates a logger, initializes the environment (CcoreFemmEnv) with parameters taken from the config including a render path inside the results directory, instantiates the A2C agent with the same config, reads and stores training parameters from the config (max_episodes, max_updates, batch_size, play_interval, save_frequency), initializes empty lists for tracking episode rewards, episode lengths, training metrics, and evaluation results, and logs an info message indicating initialization completed.

trainer::A2CTrainer::_evaluate_agent
Runs a single evaluation episode for the current agent and returns summary metrics. The method constructs a new CcoreFemmEnv using parameters from self.config (max_steps, env_dim, femm_path) and a render output directory under self.results_dir, sets the env logger to WARNING, and resets the environment. It then steps through the episode until done, choosing actions with self.agent.get_action(obs), accumulating total reward and step count, and optionally rendering each step if config['logging']['render_evaluation'] is true. After closing the environment it returns a dictionary with keys: 'reward' (total episode reward), 'length' (number of steps), and 'net_force' and 'iron_count' taken from the final step info (defaulting to 0.0 and 0 if absent).

trainer::A2CTrainer::_collect_batch
Collects a batch of experience from the environment starting at initial_obs until either self.batch_size transitions have been gathered or the episode terminates. At each step it queries self.agent.get_action(obs) to obtain an action and the agent’s value estimate for the current observation, records the observation, action, value, reward and done flag, steps the environment, and stops if done. After collection it obtains a next_value estimate for the final observation (or 0.0 if the episode ended). It returns a dictionary containing numpy arrays for observations, actions, rewards, values and dones, plus next_value, next_obs, a boolean episode_finished flag, and an iron_count extracted from the last env.info (or 0 if no steps were collected).

trainer::A2CTrainer::_compile_results
Builds and returns a summary dictionary of a completed A2C training run. Given training_time, episodes and updates counts, it collects instance attributes (self.episode_rewards, self.episode_lengths, self.training_metrics, self.evaluation_results, self.config) and packages them with the supplied counts. It also computes a final_performance sub-dictionary that contains: mean_reward_last_10 (mean of the last 10 rewards or the mean of all rewards if fewer than 10), mean_length_last_10 (same logic for episode lengths), best_reward (maximum episode reward or 0.0 if none), and final_evaluation (the last evaluation result or an empty dict if none). Means are computed using numpy.mean. The function returns this data as a Dict[str, Any].

trainer::A2CTrainer::_make_serializable
Instance method that converts Python objects containing NumPy types into JSON-serializable native Python types. It handles np.ndarray by converting to lists via tolist(), np.integer and np.floating by casting to int and float, respectively, and recursively walks dicts and lists to convert their contents. Any other objects are returned unchanged. The method is intended to prepare nested structures for JSON serialization, though it does not special-case tuples, sets or other custom types.

trainer::A2CTrainer::close
Method of A2CTrainer that performs cleanup: it calls self.env.close() to release the environment resources and logs an informational message "Trainer closed". It takes no parameters and returns None.

environment::CcoreFemmEnv
CcoreFemmEnv is a custom reinforcement-learning environment that lets an agent iteratively place magnetic material inside a discretized C‑core actuator design space and evaluates electromagnetic performance using the FEMM finite‑element tool. The environment maintains a 2D grid state (with boundary, air, copper coil, iron, and pointer IDs), a movable pointer that performs worm‑like placement (3×3 iron block) via discrete actions (directional moves), and enforces collisions/ bounds with penalties. It builds and updates a base FEMM model (coils, armature, boundaries), writes changed material blocks into the FEMM document, runs FEMM analyses, and computes a reward from the magnetic field in the armature (average B magnitude ×1000) while also extracting net force and B‑field distributions for diagnostics. Episodes are managed with reset/step semantics, history tracking (states, actions, rewards, forces, B‑fields), termination on max steps or exceeding iron count, optional data augmentation via random horizontal flip, and rendering/saving of state images. The observation returned to the agent is a local design window concatenated with the corresponding B‑field distribution (shape given by STATE_SIZE). The class exposes action_space and observation_space properties and relies on external constants (ACTIONS, MATERIAL_IDS, GEOMETRY, PENALTY, etc.) and an installed FEMM API.

environment::CcoreFemmEnv::action_space
Instance method that returns the environment's action-space size as an integer. It is a simple getter with no parameters or side effects and returns the constant ACTION_DIM.

environment::CcoreFemmEnv::_create_coils
Creates two rectangular electromagnetic coil regions in the FEMM model using geometry parameters stored on self.geometry. For the left coil it clears any existing labels/nodes/segments in the target area, draws a rectangle spanning x=[0, coil_length] and y=[coil_start, coil_start+coil_width], places a block label at the rectangle center and assigns a Copper block property with an "icoil" current of -500. For the right coil it computes a mirrored vertical position (coil2_start = 16 - (coil_start + coil_width)), similarly clears the area, draws the rectangle, adds a block label and sets a Copper block property with an "icoil" current of +500. Overall this function sets up two oppositely driven coil blocks (using the specified geometry and currents) in the FEMM environment.

environment::CcoreFemmEnv::_check_termination
Method of CcoreFemmEnv that determines whether the current episode should terminate. It takes the current state (a numpy array of material IDs), counts how many entries equal MATERIAL_IDS['iron'], and returns True if that iron count exceeds MAX_IRON. It also returns True if the environment's step_count has reached or exceeded self.max_steps. Otherwise it returns False.

environment::CcoreFemmEnv::__init__
Constructor for the C-core FEMM environment that initializes and configures the environment instance.
